newsitem.title: EGYPT: Syria says troop moves show confidence in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Syria says troop moves show confidence in Lebanon.

text.p: A Syrian troop redeployment in Lebanon reflects confidence in the Lebanese army to safeguard security in a country still recovering from its 1975-90 civil war, Syria's information minister was quoted on Tuesday as saying.

But the newspaper that carried his remarks quoted unidentified sources as saying the move was linked to expectations in Damascus that Israel would launch a military campaign against pro-Iranian guerrillas in south Lebanon.
Syria has redeployed up to 12,000 troops in Lebanon, moving some within striking distance of a key Israeli position on the Golan Heights, sparking war jitters in the Jewish state.

"The deployment of Syrian troops in Lebanon went through several stages. The general deployment at the start was to stop the killing, then during the second stage these troops were gathered in strategic positions and at checkpoints," Syrian Information Miniser Mohammad Salman told the London-based al-Hayat newspaper.

The newspaper said Salman told its editor-in-chief that the redeployment was part of a continuous operation that reflected Syria's confidence in the increasing ability of the Lebanese security forces.

But the paper quoted unidentified sources as saying the redeployment was a result of the Syrian expectation that Israel's hardline Likud government would implement an election stand to strengthen its forces in its south Lebanon occupation zone and hit Lebanese guerrillas there.

The Syrian troop redeployment has worried Israeli officials, but Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai assured Israelis on Monday there was no cause for concern but events were being closely monitored.
